scope: Named foreign shareholders (≥1%) of five NIFTY 50 constituents in batch 6 (Larsen & Toubro, Mahindra & Mahindra, Maruti Suzuki India, Max Healthcare Institute, Nestle India), from the latest available SEBI Reg. 31(1)(b) quarterly shareholding-pattern data. Two companies (Mahindra & Mahindra, quarter ended 31.12.2025; Nestle India, quarter ended 31.03.2026) were checked against the primary filing opened directly from the company's own investor-relations site. Three companies (Larsen & Toubro, Maruti Suzuki, Max Healthcare) could not be opened at their primary source within budget — L&T's IR shareholding-pattern pages are ASP.NET postback/JS with no static PDF link exposed in the HTML and every guessed direct-PDF URL pattern 404'd; Max Healthcare's IR shareholding-pattern page returned HTTP 403 to both WebFetch and a browser-UA curl; Maruti Suzuki's IR page rendered as an empty JS shell and a company-hosted Azure blob-storage PDF returned 'AccountIsDisabled' — so those three are recorded at screener.in/equitymaster.com aggregate, tier reported, with the attempted primary URLs in voids. Covers: the mandatory comparison set (BlackRock, Vanguard, NBIM/Government Pension Fund Global, GIC/Government of Singapore, Capital Group, Fidelity, Kuwait Investment Authority, ADIA, GQG Partners) tested against the two companies with primary data; LIC of India as the domestic control; two new foreign-promoter holders found in Nestle India's Table II (Nestle S.A. and its India holding vehicle Maggi Enterprises Ltd); and the pre-existing cap:suzuki-motor-corporation entity (Maruti Suzuki's promoter) carried over from research/raw/capital/holders.json with the same id/ty/fam/sz. Leaves out: adviser mandates, SEBI/RBI rule-change history and the Soros/OSF/World Bank narratives, which are out of scope for this batch file; any company outside the five named above.

symmetryCheck: Run identically across the 5 companies in this batch: LIC of India was found as a large, specifically-named domestic holder in both companies where a primary filing was opened — 10.51% of Mahindra & Mahindra and 6.14% of Nestle India — in both cases larger than any single named foreign FPI line in the same filing. BlackRock/iShares was not found named ≥1% in either primary filing. Vanguard, NBIM and GIC (the transparent, publicly-disclosing controls) appeared only in Mahindra & Mahindra, each in the 1.0–1.7% range, fragmented across share classes exactly as in the main holders.json file's 5-company sample. Where a foreign holder in this batch is genuinely large (Suzuki Motor Corporation 58.65% of Maruti Suzuki; Nestle S.A. + Maggi Enterprises Ltd 62.76% combined of Nestle India), it is a strategic/promoter industrial stake disclosed in Table II, not a passive Table III fund line — the same structural pattern already documented for British American Tobacco/ITC and Suzuki/Maruti in the main file. The lens produces a consistent picture: real large foreign ownership in Indian blue-chips is concentrated, named, strategic promoter capital, not diversified passive index funds; passive funds (BlackRock, Vanguard, NBIM, GIC) individually show up, when they show up, an order of magnitude smaller than either LIC or a strategic foreign promoter.
